# Results — Study 823 (Variance-Risk-Premium Return Predictor)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
Bollerslev, Tauchen & Zhou (2009): the **variance risk premium** (implied variance −
realized variance) **predicts the aggregate market's forward excess return**, positive
VRP → higher forward return, R² peaking at the quarterly horizon. Offline & deterministic
once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of
**2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped).
Fingerprint `b61b772dba46` (SPY close).*

*Run stamp — as-of 2026-06-30; SPY Fingerprint `b61b772dba46`; no partial months in the tape.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily closes — **SPY** (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return) + **^VIX** (index level), 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-30, **8,411** daily rows → **400** month-ends (1993-03 → 2026-06) |
| Implied variance | `IV_t = (VIX_t / 100)² / 12` at each month-end (monthly variance units) |
| Realized variance | `RV_t` = trailing-**21**-trading-day sum of daily squared **log** returns as of month-end (monthly variance units) |
| Signal | `VRP_t = IV_t − RV_t` (mean **+0.00083** monthly variance ≈ **10.0** annualised vol-points of premium — implied *does* exceed realized on average, as the literature says) |
| Forward return | `fwd_h` = SPY log return over the next `h` months (`t → t+h`); risk-free leg proxied at 0 (named on Signal axis — a near-constant bill shifts the intercept, not the slope) |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: VRP known at close of month-end `t` → hold `t → t+h`. The costed timer charges one-way × NAV per switch |
| Statistics | OLS predictive regression with a **Newey-West (HAC, Bartlett)** *t* on the slope (lags = ⌈1.5·h⌉); R²; a 2,000-draw block-bootstrap placebo; a two-era cut; a 20-seed synthetic control |

**Risk-free proxy — named on the Signal axis.** BTZ regress *excess* returns; we use SPY
total return with the bill leg set to zero. Over 1–3-month horizons a bill return is small
and near-constant, so it shifts the regression **intercept**, not the **slope** that
carries the *t*-stat. The stamp is unaffected.

## The headline — predictive regression of forward return on VRP_t

Forward `h`-month SPY log return regressed on `VRP_t` (full sample, 1993–2026):

| horizon | slope | Newey-West *t* | R² | high−low VRP tercile spread | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month | +0.41 | +0.27 | 0.12% | +0.68% | 399 |
| **3-month** | **+2.12** | **+0.75** | **1.07%** | **+2.33%** | 397 |
| 6-month | +1.45 | +0.51 | 0.23% | +2.20% | 394 |
| 12-month | −1.53 | −0.65 | 0.12% | +0.57% | 388 |

The **shape** the paper predicts is exactly here: the slope is **positive** at the short
horizons and the R² **peaks at the quarterly (3-month) horizon** (1.07%), decaying and
flipping sign by 12 months. But the **Newey-West *t* never clears 2** on the full modern
tape — at the headline 3-month horizon it is only **+0.75** (the homoskedastic OLS *t* is
+2.06; the HAC correction, which properly inflates the standard error for the persistence
and fat right tail of the VRP regressor, deflates it to +0.75). Directionally the BTZ
relation replicates; on the honest HAC bar, it does **not** certify on 1993–2026.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2010-01-01), 3-month horizon

| era | slope | Newey-West *t* | R² | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1993–2009** (brackets the paper's 1990–2007 sample) | **+7.30** | **+5.93** | **8.65%** | 199 |
| **2010–2026** | −1.84 | −1.28 | 1.27% | 195 |

Here is the whole story. In the **early** era — which spans Bollerslev-Tauchen-Zhou's own
1990–2007 window — the predictor is **strong and highly significant** (HAC *t* = +5.93,
R² = 8.65%): the edge was real. In the **late** era it **decays and inverts** (slope −1.84,
*t* = −1.28). The full-sample +0.75 is the average of a genuine early edge and a
post-publication collapse — a textbook case of an anomaly that worked in-sample and in its
original era, then faded once it was famous (the 1-month cut tells the same tale: early
*t* = +3.33, late *t* = −0.72).

## Placebo — is the (full-sample) slope a lucky alignment?

Block-rotate the forward-return series against `VRP_t` in 6-month blocks (preserving the
overlap-induced autocorrelation), 2,000 draws, 3-month horizon:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed slope | **+2.12** |
| placebo mean (sd) | −0.03 (1.06) |
| right-tail *p* | **0.024** |

The naive block rotation places the slope ~2σ into the right tail (*p* = 0.024) — but it
holds the VRP regressor **fixed**, so it does *not* capture the fat-tailed leverage of a
handful of crisis-month VRP spikes that the **HAC** standard error does. The decisive,
desk-standard read is the Newey-West *t* (+0.75) together with the era split — both of
which say the full-tape edge is **not** robust. We stamp on the HAC, not the rotation.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

Own SPY over `t → t+1` when `VRP_t` is above its expanding-window median (fat premium ⇒
own the market), else cash; one-way cost × NAV per switch, 5 bps:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| timer net Sharpe | **0.55** |
| buy-and-hold SPY Sharpe | **0.69** |
| switches / yr | 5.0 |
| fraction invested | 51% |
| timer − buy-and-hold mean return | **−0.33 %/month** (NW *t* = −2.21) |

The VRP timer **underperforms** simply owning SPY — it sits in cash half the time and gives
up **−0.33%/month** (significantly, NW *t* = −2.21) for the privilege, churning 5×/yr. Even
the version that worked in-sample does not translate into a directional market-timer you
would rather hold than the index. **Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded SPY+VIX tape with a planted VRP (`IV = RV + vrp_m` by construction)
and — only when `edge > 0` — a forward mean return that loads `+edge` on `VRP_t`. No
network. 3-month horizon, 20 seeds:

| world | predictive slope | HAC *t* | R² | fires (\|t\|≥2) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | +0.84 | **+0.28** | 0.3% | **0/20** |
| planted (`edge = 6`), **20 seeds** | +12.57 | **+3.95** | 6.6% | **20/20** |

The detector recovers a *planted* BTZ relation cleanly and never fires on the null — so the
weak full-tape *t* and the sharp early/late split are genuine features of the real tape, not
a broken engine. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the
real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The Bollerslev-Tauchen-Zhou predictor's **shape replicates** — the
  slope is positive and the R² peaks at the quarterly horizon exactly as claimed, and it is
  **strongly significant in the original era** (1993–2009: HAC *t* = **+5.93**, R² = 8.65%).
  But on the **full modern tape the Newey-West *t* is only +0.75** (< 2) and the edge
  **decays and inverts** after 2010 (*t* = −1.28). Right sign, right horizon, real in its
  time — but not certifiable out-of-sample. Amber, not green.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** A VRP-conditioned market-timer **loses to buy-and-hold** SPY
  (Sharpe 0.55 vs 0.69; mean −0.33%/month, NW *t* = −2.21).
- **In-sample vs out-of-sample — DECAYED.** A ~6-*t* edge in 1993–2009 collapses to an
  insignificant, wrong-signed −1.28 in 2010–2026 — a post-publication fade, the desk's
  recurring lesson.
